findings.reason: The protected place-value source uses the prohibited local name index. The inert candidate preserves the exact decimal-block arithmetic and app-local contract while using the conventional digit-position variable i.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 400 and its Python findNthDigit surface. The Reference preserves the one-based position in the concatenated positive-integer sequence, the decimal-digit return range, both source examples in order with the supplied explanation complete, and the full positive 32-bit position constraint.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064709014 and uses the same width-block subtraction, zero-based offset, containing-number calculation, and place-value extraction as the protected app-local source. The candidate is inert and changes only the final digit-position name.

The legal 2-, 5-, and 9-decimal-width tiers span 4.5x in the logarithmic workload and remain below the signed 32-bit position maximum. The candidate passes all 11 executions at -0.03 relative growth and 1.00x; correct binary search with repeated cumulative-width counting passes every output but fails only scaling at +0.93 and 7.08x.

The Approach matches the candidate's i notation, derives each fixed-width block size, explains the n - 1 boundary conversion, identifies the containing number by quotient and position by remainder, and proves O(log n) time with O(1) space.

The hash-bound public Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including the infinite positive-integer sequence, one-based digit objective, both source examples in order, the explanation for the zero in 10, and the exact input range.
